title: How Far Crypto Has Come in Washington - a16z crypto
gist: a16z crypto's policy head argues the Clarity Act's failure to clear the Senate is a setback but not an empty-handed outcome: GENIUS is law, key hostile rules were rescinded, and SEC/CFTC are building the framework by rulemaking, leaving durability as the remaining problem.

insights.claim: The US now has a federal stablecoin law (GENIUS) with issuer requirements and customer protections, and agencies are in the implementation phase rather than debating whether crypto legislation can pass.
insights.speaker: Collin McCune
insights.so_what: Stablecoin regulation is now an implementation story; watch agency rulemaking and other jurisdictions copying the model.

insights.claim: Congress overturned the IRS DeFi broker rule, the SEC rescinded SAB 121, and FinCEN withdrew the Unhosted Wallet Rule, removing three major barriers to US crypto business models.
insights.speaker: Collin McCune
insights.so_what: Lower compliance overhang for institutional custody and DeFi software builders in the US.
insights.locator: That's just the most visible achievement

insights.claim: The House has passed comprehensive market-structure legislation twice with bipartisan support, FIT21 in 2024 and Clarity in 2025, but Clarity has not passed the Senate.
insights.speaker: Collin McCune
insights.so_what: Senate passage is the binding constraint on durable market-structure law; treat timing as uncertain.

insights.claim: The SEC has proposed a token-offering framework and crypto custody rules, and issued an exemption letting certain tokenized stocks trade onchain, while the CFTC proposed a path to regulate centralized exchanges.
insights.speaker: Collin McCune
insights.so_what: Tokenized equities and regulated exchanges are advancing via agencies even without Clarity; track exemptions and final rules.
insights.locator: Then there's the proactive work happening at the agencies

insights.claim: SEC and CFTC guidance now answers core operating questions: how to launch a token, how it can trade, and who may hold customer assets with what obligations.
insights.speaker: Collin McCune
insights.so_what: Clearer token launch and custody rules reduce legal risk premia for US-based crypto projects.
insights.locator: These are also central to Clarity

insights.claim: Proposed rules, guidance and exemptions are not final and can shift with each presidential election, so only legislation or durable rulemaking gives companies a ten-year investment foundation.
insights.speaker: Collin McCune
insights.so_what: Regulatory regime-change risk persists until Clarity or equivalent passes; a political turnover is the key downside scenario.
insights.quote: A company making a ten-year investment would understandably like to know that the rules won’t depend on the outcome of every presidential election.

insights.claim: The author frames the regulatory problem as having shifted from 'can we build in America at all' under the SEC enforcement era to 'making progress last', and says founders no longer plan around leaving the US.
insights.speaker: Collin McCune
insights.so_what: Reduced regulatory flight risk is a supportive backdrop for US crypto venture and listings.
